title: Investigate skill fast/deep split
summary: The investigate skill's investigator agent runs a 5-step pipeline. Step 4 (Bounded expansion — adjacent_facts) spawns 3-5 extra sub-investigations to surface adjacent material facts. This is always-on today and accounts for meaningful latency. The decision: split fast vs deep modes gated entirely on whether step 4 runs. Steps 1-3 are identical in both modes. The investigate skill will always present an AskUserQuestion prompt (header: Depth) before routing to the investigator; explicit 'fast' or 'deep' in the user's message skips the prompt. A new `depth: fast|deep` field is added to the investigator Input contract. Absent → deep, preserving current behavior for direct callers (pr-revise, pr-code-review). The field is universal — any caller may pass it. A one-line skip guard at the top of step 4 enforces fast mode. Fast/deep guidance is documented in investigator.md as a non-binding rule: fast for one self-contained falsifiable fact; deep for act-on-context, triage, why/how, or multi-claim.
decisions: Lever is step 4 (Bounded expansion — adjacent_facts) on/off only. Steps 1-3 run identically in both modes.
Control surface is AskUserQuestion in the investigate skill — no typed flag. User taps, not types.
Skill always presents fast/deep prompt. Explicit 'fast' or 'deep' in the user's request skips the prompt and honors the explicit choice.
depth: fast|deep field added to investigator agent Input contract. Absent → deep. Preserves current always-on behavior for all existing callers.
Step 4 gains a one-line skip guard: if depth == fast, skip step 4 and proceed to step 5. Step 5 is unchanged (adjacent_facts already optional in schema).
depth field is universal — any caller may pass it at any call-site. Not restricted to the investigate skill.
Direct callers (pr-revise, pr-code-review) do not change today. They pass no depth field → default deep. They may add depth: fast at specific call-sites in the future.

Fast/deep line documented as guidance in investigator.md: fast = one self-contained falsifiable fact where adjacent context won't change the action; deep = act-on-context, incident triage, why/how, or multi-claim.

AskUserQuestion prompt: header 'Depth', question 'Fast or deep answer?', Fast listed first (Literal answer only, verdict+evidence, skips adjacent-facts, fewer spawns, quicker), Deep listed second (Full investigation + adjacent facts, more spawns, slower).
implementation_decisions: agents/investigator.md: add `depth` (optional, enum fast|deep, default deep) to the Input section.
agents/investigator.md: add skip guard at top of step 4 — 'If depth == fast, skip this step and proceed to step 5.'
agents/investigator.md: add fast/deep guidance block near step 4 or in a preamble, non-binding, per the documented line.

skills/investigate/SKILL.md: add Step 0 (or inline after input parse) — spawn AskUserQuestion with header 'Depth', 'Fast or deep answer?', Fast/Deep options. Honor explicit 'fast'/'deep' in $ARGUMENTS to skip prompt.
skills/investigate/SKILL.md: append `depth: fast` or `depth: deep` to the investigator prompt string based on user selection.
next_action: Run /to-tasks to generate the implementation task file for the two-file change.
further_notes: Both files are under ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/ — investigator.md under agents/, SKILL.md under skills/investigate/.
The investigate skill already parses --out raw|slack in Step 0. The depth prompt is a separate concern and should be its own step or a parallel parse in the same step.
No changes to the investigation-result schema are needed — adjacent_facts is already optional/omittable.
